_about: 737-600, from Boeing D6-58325-7 Rev C (October 2025) 2.2.1 (page index 29): side, plan and front views on one sheet, drawn about 3.5% smaller than the 737-700W's and in thinner lines. Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 14, line centres (side_all.png: fills and the blue strokes of doors and cockpit panes together). The 737-700's points moved by the two plugs (plug.py), then snapped; the fin, the plain wing tip, the wing and the nacelle placed here (this sheet draws them a little differently from the 737-700W's).

windows.note: Boeing's drawing has no cabin windows: placed at the 737's 20 in (0.508 m) frame pitch, on the overwing exit's window, from the first door to the aft door; their height is the 737-800's (the same fuselage section).

sources.title: Boeing, 737-600/-700/-800/-900 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58325-7 Rev C, October 2025), 2.2.1 General Dimensions: Model 737-600
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b736/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Plain wing tips, as the sheet draws them (few 737-600s carry winglets). The drawing has no cabin windows: they're placed at the 737's frame pitch on the overwing exit, at the 737-800's height. The eyebrow windows are left out, as on the 737-700 and -800. The side view draws the engine's inlet lip 9.08 m from the nose where the sheet prints 8.84 m (its plan view draws it at 9.38 m): the nacelle is moved 0.24 m forward to the printed figure (build.py, as for any inlet more than 1.5% off). This sheet also draws the fin about 0.3 m further aft on the tail cone than the 737-700W's sheet does; kept as drawn.
